source.title: We Inspected Every Head In GPT-2 Small using SAEs So You Don’t Have To

record.tranche_reason: The study reports results about GPT-2 Small attention-head polysemanticity, not about neurons or MLP neurons named in the claim versions. It therefore does not test or use the claim as defined.
record.gate_note: The reported polysemanticity counts and H10.2 ablations concern attention heads, a related but different construct; recorded under fits_no_version. The long-prefix induction experiments are omitted because they examine induction-head specialization, not polysemanticity.
record.test_reason: The study measures polysemanticity of attention heads in GPT-2 Small via attention-layer SAE features, not of MLP neurons or vision-model neurons. Head polysemanticity is a related but different construct, so no claim version is tested; the findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors also note that head polysemanticity is a spectrum, and that features rather than heads may be better units of analysis.
record.recipe_differences: Uses attention-layer SAEs and decoder-weight attribution to group features by attention head, rather than the original source's neuron visualization and interpretation approach.
record.method_sensitivity: The interpretation is limited to the top 10 features per head, ranked by decoder-weight attribution; the authors note that this is an imperfect proxy and recommend FVE for reproductions. They also note that the boundary between mono- and polysemantic heads is blurry.

fits_no_version.finding: Over 90% of GPT-2 Small attention heads appear to perform multiple tasks under top-10 SAE feature grouping. Of 144 heads, 14 are plausibly monosemantic, 8 mostly monosemantic and 4 plausibly bisemantic.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Most attention heads in small transformer language models are polysemantic at the head level, with a small minority of plausibly monosemantic heads.

fits_no_version.finding: Zero-ablating H10.2 raises mean loss clearly more than ablating other Layer 10 heads, on both integer-copying and URL-completion synthetic datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Individual attention heads can causally contribute to multiple unrelated tasks.

record.problems: The authors inspect only the top 10 features per head using an imperfect attribution proxy, report that the review of head examples was shallow, and acknowledge possible false positives and false negatives. The text does not provide numerical ablation values or uncertainty estimates for the H10.2 results.
record.rows_left_out: No further results bearing on neuron polysemanticity were reported. Long-prefix induction results were left out because they concern specialization of attention heads, not polysemanticity.

untested.parts: No MLP neurons measured; only attention heads in GPT-2 Small.
Superposition as a cause of neuron polysemanticity is not tested; attention head superposition is only mentioned as a limitation.
No test of polysemanticity without capacity pressure.
No comparison across architectures, activation functions or regularization.
No reassessment of canonical polysemantic neurons. The H5.10 'context head' remark concerns heads, not neurons.
The blurry mono/polysemantic boundary and top-10 caveats concern heads, not neuron activation ranges or explanation scoring.

record.verdict_notes: The rows are accurately extracted and correctly linked to no version. One wording slip: the text says 'top 10 features' in places where a reader might expect 'top 10 attributed features', and the 9.7% figure versus the '9%' in the introduction is a rounding difference only. Leaving out the long-prefix induction results is appropriate.

versions.untested_parts: The study examines language-model attention heads, not neurons in image classifiers.
It does not measure MLP neurons or their responses to unrelated tokens or contexts.
It does not test whether neuron polysemanticity is caused by superposition or feature-to-neuron capacity pressure.
It does not test neuron polysemanticity arising from initialization, regularization, or training noise when capacity is sufficient.
It does not compare neuron polysemanticity across architectures, activation functions, or regularization settings.
It does not reassess canonical polysemantic neurons or test whether their mixed inputs share a feature.
Its measurement caveats concern attention-head feature attribution, not how neuron polysemanticity varies with activation range or explanation scoring.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: Manually grouped each head's top 10 SAE-attributed features by conceptual relatedness
rows.measure: Share of heads judged plausibly monosemantic because all top 10 features were conceptually related
rows.locator: Investigating Attention Head Polysemanticity; Discovering Plausibly Monosemantic Heads
rows.note: This is a head-level judgment based on a small, ranked set of SAE features; the authors say it cannot prove monosemanticity.
